evidence_text: Then I called the company and asked why my smart rules did not work… they were set to work for only one day because I did not have an end date… Now I have to get back on track again and try to believe that I can make the lights work.
supports: Need to understand and sustain automation behavior and recover from configuration failure.
does_not_support: Does not establish a population-wide need or a final lighting responsibility.

evidence_text: I could see when our house cleaner came and went. Something I checked a few times but always had a bad conscience about doing…
supports: Remote household visibility created a privacy, trust, and legitimacy conflict.
does_not_support: Does not establish total rejection of monitoring or generalize to all households.

evidence_text: Very strange. Today at 11 o’clock, I started to think that it was a bit cold… it was set to ‘not at home’… programmed to ‘not-home’ during daytime on Thursdays and Fridays.
authorship_or_status: diary author reporting lived use during changed work context
supports: Old occupancy schedules can conflict with current household context; state and rationale need to be inspectable.
does_not_support: Does not specify a preferred temperature or prove a later resolution.

evidence_text: I still have not downloaded the app that allows me to track our consumption and to see when energy prices are low, although I am in principle interested in it.
supports: Stated interest in energy information did not translate into actual tool adoption.
does_not_support: Does not support that price-aware charging was practiced or requested as an automation.

evidence_text: The paper describes morning/evening lighting rules, motion-triggered lighting when the resident woke at night, and the resident's use of lighting for relaxation and reading.
authorship_or_status: many rules created by resident's son/caregiver
supports: Within one household, lighting mechanisms were associated with daily rhythm, nighttime activity, and relaxation/reading.
does_not_support: Does not show that every rule directly expressed the older resident's own need or produced clinical benefit.

evidence_text: The paper describes negotiated rules to turn on lights after morning inactivity, illuminate under low-light conditions, and periodically remind cognitive training, eye drops, and drinking water.
supports: State- and time-conditioned support was used for morning routines, lighting, and recurring health-related activities.
does_not_support: Does not establish independent authorship or long-term adherence for each rule.

evidence_text: I have had my watch for 20 years and I don't want to take it off or even put a new one on me.
context: A professional caregiver also sought tablet glucose reminders and nighttime bed-motion-triggered bathroom lighting.
supports: The resident expressed a clear wearable-technology boundary while the caregiver pursued other care automations.
does_not_support: Caregiver goals cannot be treated as confirmed resident responsibilities; does not generalize to older adults.

evidence_text: The paper describes medication and cognitive-training reminders plus lighting control; the resident used pink lighting when sad, described it as relaxing, and considered game reminders helpful for training and learning tablet use.
authorship_or_status: field deployment and reported participant experience
supports: Personalized light and recurring reminders were experienced as support for mood, training, and technology learning.
does_not_support: Does not establish medical efficacy or a universal responsibility category.

evidence_text: If tomorrow's weather forecast says it will rain and if there is an event scheduled in the Google Calendar app, then preset to close the windows tomorrow and send a text warning the person to take precautions for the rain.
supports: A participant imagined combining forecast, calendar, preparation, and notification.
does_not_support: Not deployed or executed; the intended precautions and persistence are not established.

evidence_text: If no one is home, FILL the dog bowl with water if it is below the indicated level and turn ON the security cameras
supports: A participant imagined absence-conditioned pet care and monitoring actions.
does_not_support: Does not establish actual pet ownership, deployment, monitoring consent, or a unique shared purpose for both actions.

evidence_text: If the house temperature is not higher than 17°, TURN UP the heating and CHECK the air humidity level, if humidity <35% ACTIVATE the humidifier
supports: A participant imagined sequential temperature and humidity control rather than a single action.
does_not_support: Does not establish safe or stable thresholds, deployment, or a validated HVAC policy.

evidence_text: When a certain food is missing in the fridge, send a notification and add the product to the shopping list on the fridge LED.
supports: A participant imagined linking food state, notification, and shopping-list maintenance.
does_not_support: Does not establish sensing feasibility, real use, or whether the higher-level purpose is organization, convenience, or something else.
